author: agent-3
reviewStatus: AUTHORED SOLO in response to A2's v1 rejection. Not re-reviewed.
purpose: Fix the durable logical Plan contract: a two-level boundary, compound Coverage keys, a testable operator-equivalence harness, mechanical capability denial, and requiredness that cannot yield a false pass.

resolves.A2-C2-V1-01: Two-level model adopted. An outer InvocationPlan covers pre-analysis host work (config resolution, admission, contribution resolution, snapshot capture, PlanId allocation). The inner ExecutionPlan is snapshot-bound and contains NO snapshot stage. The five kinds are now exhaustive for the inner Plan, which is what they were always plausibly exhaustive for.
resolves.A2-C2-V1-02: Coverage is keyed by the compound tuple (relation, language/semanticUniverseId, subject-scope partition), with per-consumer consumption status. The mixed-language counterexample is now representable and is included as a test.
resolves.A2-C2-V1-03: PS-07 rewritten: ONE public Plan fed to a test-only physical planner forced into two operator strategies. Equality preconditions stated — exact Coverage first, then digest. Resolves the contradiction where two public Plans differed in private operators.
resolves.A2-C2-V1-04: Enum labelling cannot prove capability limits, so PS-09 is a runtime capability-DENIAL test: a rule-evaluation stage attempting process, network, or filesystem access fails, whatever it is labelled.
resolves.A2-C2-V1-05: Requiredness made explicit. A fault or budget exhaustion in a REQUIRED rule becomes a Coverage entry and forces indeterminate. Only optional-rule faults are isolated.

twoLevelPlan.why: v1 said the Snapshotter precedes the Planner and simultaneously listed a snapshot stage inside the Plan. Both cannot be true. The repair is to name the outer level rather than to delete the stage.

InvocationPlan.isNotAStage: These are pre-analysis host activities. They are not Plan stages because they must complete before a snapshot-bound Plan can exist at all — a Plan is defined relative to a SnapshotId.
InvocationPlan.failureBefore: Any failure here is pre-admission: request-rejected or operational, never a Run verdict.

ExecutionPlan.custody: public contract; may be selected by a data-only profile
ExecutionPlan.boundTo: exactly one SnapshotId and one PlanId
ExecutionPlan.exhaustiveness: Closed for the inner Plan. An unknown kind is rejected, not ignored. A fifth public kind is a Plan schema major (see versioning-policy CONSUMER-CUSTODY).

twoLevelPlan.note: The snapshot stage listed in v1 becomes an InvocationPlan activity. The inner kind count therefore drops from five to four.

coverageKey.why: A single record per relation cannot say 'resolved-complete for TypeScript, unavailable for Go' in one Plan. Per-relation was necessary and not sufficient.

consumerStatus.rule: Every rule and query records its status against the EXACT Coverage entries it consumed, not against a Plan-level summary.

coverageKey.languageTierLink: A syntax-tier language produces unavailable resolved-relation entries with reason COVERAGE.LANGUAGE_TIER_UNSUPPORTED — the mechanism by which the P-4 loud-tier decision becomes observable rather than editorial.

requiredness.rule: Every rule in a Plan is REQUIRED or OPTIONAL, declared, never defaulted silently.
requiredness.requiredFault: A fault or budget exhaustion in a REQUIRED rule becomes a Coverage entry and forces policy indeterminate.
requiredness.optionalFault: Isolated, recorded as a diagnostic and a Coverage entry; does not force indeterminate.
requiredness.whyThisWasABlocker: v1 said 'rule fault is isolated and does not fail the plan.' Applied to a required rule that permits a passing verdict from an analysis that did not run — the exact false pass the sealed invariant forbids.

privateOperators.rule: MUST NOT appear in the public ExecutionPlan schema.
privateOperators.plannerFreedom: Insert, reorder, fuse, or elide freely, provided the logical stage contract and the resulting EvidenceDigest are unchanged under identical exact Coverage.

domainResults.queryNeverRunsAnalysis: A query against a stored fact view returns a typed unavailable response naming the missing requirement. Only explicit admission creates a Run.

conformanceTests.assert: Every stage kind in a serialised ExecutionPlan is one of the four declared kinds. An unknown kind is rejected.
No serialised ExecutionPlan contains any private operator. Round-tripping loses no logical information.
Coverage entries carry the full compound key. A Plan over TypeScript and Go reports resolved-complete for TypeScript and unavailable for Go in the same Run.
A rule whose declared requirements are unmet records skipped-requirements-unmet and is never evaluated against insufficient facts.
Budget exhaustion in rule-evaluation and provider unavailability in fact-derivation produce distinct Coverage reason codes.
A query against a fact view lacking required relations returns typed unavailable and creates no Run.

ONE schema-identical public ExecutionPlan is executed by a test-only physical planner forced into two distinct operator strategies. Assert exact Coverage identical FIRST; then assert EvidenceDigest equality. If the strategies exhaust different budgets, exact Coverage differs and the digest comparison is not performed — a Coverage divergence is reported instead.
A profile may raise a fact-quality floor; no profile label alone triggers materialisation.

CAPABILITY DENIAL: a stage labelled rule-evaluation that attempts process spawn, network, or filesystem access is denied at runtime and the attempt is recorded. Labelling does not confer authority, and mislabelling does not obtain it.
A REQUIRED rule that faults or exhausts its budget forces policy indeterminate. An OPTIONAL one does not.
An ExecutionPlan containing a snapshot stage is rejected — snapshot capture is InvocationPlan work.
Effectful work is representable only as a probe stage. A rule-evaluation stage requesting probe grants is rejected at plan validation, before execution.

sealedPropertiesCovered.property: required partial coverage cannot yield pass
effectful work is unrepresentable as a Rule
the language capability tier is observable

peerReviewRequired: Is the InvocationPlan / ExecutionPlan split the right repair, versus moving snapshot capture wholly outside any plan concept? A2 flagged medium confidence on which repair is better and this artifact chose one.
Is the three-part Coverage key sufficient, or does subject-scope partition need further decomposition for cross-file relations?
Does PS-09 belong here or in the capability matrix? It is a runtime property being asserted by a plan-schema artifact.
knownLimitations: Field-level schemas for the four stage kinds are still unspecified.
PS-07 requires a test-only physical planner harness that does not exist; the test is specified, not implemented.
PS-09 assumes a runtime capability-denial mechanism the architecture requires but no artifact designs.

Dropping the inner kind count from five to four is a change to a previously reviewed shape; A2 approved five kinds for a Plan that included snapshot. The reduction follows from the two-level split but has not been re-reviewed.
